name: DeckCraft
summary: Edit PowerPoint presentations in Nextcloud with DeckCraft
description:
Open a PowerPoint (.pptx, .potx, .ppsx) or DeckCraft presentation in Files with **Edit in DeckCraft** and work on it right in the browser: themes, layouts, shapes, pictures, tables, charts, transitions, animations, speaker notes and the slide show.

- **Save** stores the presentation in DeckCraft's own format next to the original the first time (you pick the name and folder), and to that file from then on. **File › Export › PowerPoint** writes the .pptx back, and Nextcloud keeps the previous state as a file version.
- **Export** (PDF, PNG, JPEG, outline) stores a file in any folder you pick.
- Read-only files open normally; saving offers a copy.
- If someone else changes the file while you have it open, you choose whether to replace their version or save a copy.
- Optionally, clicking a presentation in Files opens it in DeckCraft.
readme_features:
- **Edit in DeckCraft** appears in the Files action menu of every PowerPoint (.pptx, .potx, .ppsx) and DeckCraft (.deckcraft) presentation you can read.
- **Save** (Ctrl/⌘+S) stores the presentation in DeckCraft's own format: the first time, you pick the name and folder (it's offered next to the original), and later saves go to that file. **File › Export › PowerPoint** writes the .pptx back under its own name. Nextcloud keeps the previous state of a file as a version.
- **Export** (PDF, PNG, JPEG, outline) asks for a name and folder in your Nextcloud the first time.
readme_limitations: - In the browser DeckCraft saves in its own format (.deckcraft); PowerPoint files are written with **File › Export › PowerPoint**.
bridge_notes: With `?host=parent`, DeckCraft starts without the sample deck, an optional `&author=<name>` signs the user's comments, and the parent guards leaving the page with unsaved changes. A presentation handed to the parent (DeckCraft, PowerPoint) counts as saved.
